kata.name: Singleton missing instance - zero Engine rows parses and check emits nothing; absence surfaces only as per-cell dangling and an empty-arrow key is refused at parse (null result; named missing law)
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md Singleton row (unexpressible: unique element - object identity has no predicate); fixtures/katas/singleton/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.7
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: an object with no rows is legal data, so the primary fixture parses and check emits 0 findings while the conventional count test names the absence; on the dangling variant the kernel's two dangling findings are per accessor cell and the baseline identifies the same element (parity). The empty-arrow key probe shows the only syntactic route to an at-most-one claim is refused. Killed with the missing existence constraint named.

expected.detail: The instance declares no Engine rows and no clients; the document parses (every declared object may have an empty row list) and check emits 0 findings. There is no non-emptiness or exact-cardinality constraint on an object's row set. The conventional arm counts the rows (singleton:engine-missing).

On missing-instance-dangling.ct.json one client's engine and fallback cells are null; check emits two dangling findings, one per cell. The baseline's accessor-resolution assertion identifies the same element, so this is parity on the per-cell surface, not an object-level cardinality check.

empty-key.ct.json declares a key with an empty arrow tuple - the only syntactic form that would mean at most one Engine row. The parser refuses the document (invalid_key: an injectivity claim needs at least one arrow), recorded as an executed construction probe, not a finding.

commands: python3 prototype/singleton_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: primary yields singleton:engine-missing; dangling variant adds singleton:accessor-dangling@Client#0
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/singleton/missing-instance.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/singleton/missing-instance-dangling.ct.json --json  # exit 4, 2 dangling
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/singleton/empty-key.ct.json --json  # exit 1, invalid_key (see probes)

probes.name: empty-key-refused

equations.rationale: every access path returns the same singleton row
the client observes the singleton's current mode

probes.observed: invalid_key: key declares no arrows: an injectivity claim needs at least one arrow

comparison.conventional_baseline: scripted conventional singleton test: exactly one Engine row (count assertion), every accessor resolving to a declared Engine row and naming the same row, mode coherence; the probe document is not an instance and is never run through the baseline arm

baseline.artifact: prototype/singleton_baseline.py sha256:ff109499c871f2b8361c809daddac175dcac9b805d8227aa938864e8479f5873 (scripted conventional singleton test; executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: the instance contains at least one row of every declared singleton object (existence, |rows(Engine)| >= 1)
expressibility_gap.why: there is no non-emptiness constraint on an object's row set: the empty instance is legal by design and parses cleanly, and the only kernel trace of absence is a null accessor cell (a per-cell dangling finding), which is data-dependent and silent when no client row references the object

expressibility_gap.invariant: at most one row of the declared singleton object (|rows(Engine)| <= 1)
expressibility_gap.why: keys require a non-empty arrow tuple and are injectivity over value tuples; a key with an empty tuple is refused at parse (invalid_key), so the degenerate at-most-one claim has no spelling on the surface

discrepancies: A conventional count test names the missing instance; the kernel names only the null accessor cells when a client row exists, and nothing when no row references the object. This is a null result with the missing existence predicate named, not a probe advantage.
procedure: 1. The law was named before any fixture: exact cardinality / unique element, |rows(Engine)| = 1 with every access path resolving to that row (fixtures/katas/singleton/README.md).
2. The conventional arm (prototype/singleton_baseline.py, sha256 above) ran first: exactly-one row, accessor resolution and row identity, and mode coherence, over the frozen fault set.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`; the construction probe is the same binary refusing an unparseable document.

4. Witnesses were mapped to the pre-registered element vocabulary; unique = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. A key collision and a row count resolve to the same element (the duplicate); a construction rejection is recorded, never counted.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed (parity or null); the cardinality half is recorded in expressibility_gap, never invented as a finding.

6. Verdict: no executed probe element falls outside the baseline's set, so unique is empty and the entry is killed; the construction rejection is recorded in run.probes and never counted. The missing existence constraint is the named missing law.
